name: Proxima Centauri b
notes: The closest known exoplanet to our Solar System, orbiting within its star's habitable zone — though intense stellar flares from its red-dwarf host raise open questions about surface habitability.

name: TRAPPIST-1e
notes: One of seven roughly Earth-sized planets orbiting an ultra-cool red dwarf; among the most Earth-sized and rocky of the seven, and a leading target for atmospheric study with JWST.

name: Kepler-186f
notes: The first validated Earth-sized planet found orbiting within another star's habitable zone.

name: 51 Pegasi b
notes: The first exoplanet confirmed orbiting a Sun-like star, and the archetype of the 'hot Jupiter' class — a giant planet orbiting extremely close to its star. Its discovery earned the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics.

name: HD 209458 b
notes: Nicknamed 'Osiris' — the first exoplanet confirmed via the transit method, and the first found to have an atmosphere, which was detected escaping the planet due to intense stellar heating.

name: WASP-12b
notes: An extreme hot Jupiter orbiting so close to its star that it is being gradually pulled apart, feeding a disk of material onto its star.
